To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
sample size is needed to achieve acceptable error in values, and that the amount of error is a function of the sample size and the amount of variability in responses.

(1) the amount of acceptable error is determined by users and is not a statistical concept, (2) acceptable error is not the same as being within an acceptable percentage, for example 5%, (3) sample sizes needed to achieve a certain amount of acceptable error are large and depend on the variability of responses, (4) sample sizes needed are not affected by the size of the population being estimated, and (5) small samples can provide useful information if the acceptable error is not very

sample size is a key determinant of acceptable error in tourism surveys, and that the amount of acceptable error is a function of the sample size, variability in responses, and the desired precision (i.e., acceptable amount of error) of the estimate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to use the information in tourism surveys.
how to achieve acceptable accuracy and reliability for values estimated from a sample survey.
how to achieve acceptable error and how to interpret estimates from tourism surveys.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a sample size of 10,000 is needed to have a total expenditure estimate within $10 million of the true value with 95% certainty.
a sample size of 10,000 is needed to achieve an acceptable error of ±5% for the total of a variable that is distributed in a normal fashion and is not skewed.
the larger the sample size, the more accurate the estimate, the smaller the variability, the smaller the acceptable amount of error that can be achieved.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the sample size needed to estimate a total to an acceptable level of error is a function of the acceptable error, the coefficient of variation of the data, the confidence level, the design effect, and the number of strata.
for many applications, sample sizes for tourism surveys need to be larger than is commonly believed to be necessary.
sample sizes of about 5000 to 10,000 are needed to achieve acceptable error of 5% or 10% for many estimates from tourism surveys.
The main takeaway from our work is that
estimates from surveys are not accurate, but can be reliable, and the reliability can be expressed in terms of acceptable error.
sample sizes needed to achieve an acceptable amount of sampling error for means and totals are much larger than is commonly understood.
estimates from tourism surveys can be accurate, but the amount of acceptable error is determined by the sample size, not by the survey itself.
